newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria shares up with helping hand from Flughafen.
newsitem.headline: Austria shares up with helping hand from Flughafen.

text.p: Austrian shares closed 0.79 percent higher on Monday, helped by a sharp rebound in Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien, and traders said they were optimistic the ATX index would continue its advance.
The index of 21 blue chips gained 8.79 points on healthy volume to finish at 1,127.08. Overall 16 shares were up, three down and two unchanged.
"The market has shored up the 1,120 points level and the upward trend is intact," said a trader.
Some Austrian banks said the ATX had potential to rally towards 1,200 points, others were more cautious. "That's still a long way off," said one, warning against early euphoria.
Buying interest extended beyond a few big names to the less liquid shares. "The ones that got left behind at the end of last week are playing catch-up," said a dealer.
Flughafen Wien was the day's biggest gainer, soaring almost nine percent in early trade before drifting back. Flughafen finished 5.05 percent, or 25 schillings, up at 520 schillings.
Market participants said demand from foreign investors, including some funds, was behind Flughafen's rebound. In November the stock touched a year-low of 473 schillings.
Industrial group Radex-Heraklith, paper maker Mayr-Melnhof and building materials firm Wienerberger also finished in positive territory.
Ordinary shares in Creditanstalt-Bankverein bucked the generally positive trend to end 0.69 percent down at 724 schillings -- the day's biggest decliner.
Creditanstalt shares are locked within a few schillings of the price an international consortium around EA-Generali has reportedly bid for the bank.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index firmed 2.66 points to 426.56. December ATX futures stood 6.4 points up at 1,124.3. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254
